title: Listing enrolled devices: page size and how each SDK pages

prose.text: The device list is paged, and the two SDKs page it differently. A device missing from a list read is not evidence that it is not enrolled until the read is known to be complete.

prose.label: The API.
prose.text: The page parameters and their defaults are [[zcc.api.devices-wire:api-page-size]].

prose.label: Go.
prose.text: {{go-getall}} Whether a page can come back shorter than requested before the end is open {{gap:short-page-before-end}}. The general consequence of a truncated list read is in [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination:truncated-list-reads-as-absent-object]].

checks.do: For a Python read, whether the caller walked every page, since one call returns one page of 50 by default.
For a Go read, whether the count is a multiple of 1000 or ended on a short page that could be a server cap.

go-getall.statement: The Go `devices.GetAll` always requests pages of 1000 starting at page 1 and stops at the first page with fewer than 1000 devices; the caller cannot change the page size.

python-one-page.statement: The Python `list_devices` makes one request with the caller's parameters and returns that response's page; with no page size given it lets the API use its default of 50. A given size is sent as given; the SDK clamps it to 1 through 5000 only for the limit its response object uses to decide whether there is a next page.
python-one-page.conditions: Corrected per verifier: the clamp runs on the response object after the request is sent and sets only the limit that has_next compares against, so it does not change the requested page size.

short-page-before-end.title: Whether the device list can return a short page before the last one
short-page-before-end.detail: The contract allows pages of up to 5000, so a Go page of 1000 should be full until the end; whether the server ever caps a page lower, which would make the Go read stop early and report success, is not stated.
